# PART 2 – The claim and its estimand {.darkslide background-color="rgba(0,0,0,0)"}

::: {.partlabel}
Part 2 – 90 minutes
:::

::: notes
Part two. The case of the day is an experiment, and an unusually clean one: emails that differed only in the name that signed them, sent to housing authorities at random. Five analysts in Multi100 reanalysed one of its claims from the same public file and still parted company, on the size of the effect and even on whether there was evidence for it. This part explains how that can happen. We go inside the paper first, then step back to two studies that show how often disagreement among analysts is disagreement about the question. Then we build the two tools that state a question precisely, the estimand and the causal graph, and use both on our claim, where the graph turns up something that is easy to miss.
:::
